To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel nitric oxide releasing spirolactone type diterpenoid compounds were designed and synthesized, and their cytotoxicity against human cancer cell lines and their NO releasing property and apoptotic inducing ability were studied.
the novel NO-releasing spirollactone-type diperpenoid derivatives (15a-f) exhibited potent in vitro anticancer activity against Bel-7402 cell line via mitochondria-related apoptosis pathway.
a series of novel nitroso-derivatives were synthesized and evaluated in vitro for their cytotoxic, NO releasing and apoptosis inducing activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a series of novel NO-releasing spirotetronate-type diterpenoids.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of a series of novel nitrospirolactone-type analogues of diterpenoids.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of a novel series of nitric oxide-releasable spirolactone derivatives (10a-d and 15a-d) as anticancer agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NO-releasing spiroleptone-type diterpene analogs 10a-f and15a-f exhibited potent anticancer activity, especially compounds 15d and 15e, with the IC50 values of 0.9-3.8μM.
the NO-releasing spirollactone-type diperenoid derivatives could be considered as potential anticancer agents.
the NO-releasing spirollactone-type dierpenoids could be a promising anticancer agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a series of novel nitroso-spirolactone-type analogs of diterpenoid, and these compounds showed significant antiproliferation activity and NO-releasing ability, and the mechanism study showed that these NO-releasing compounds could induce apoptosis via mitochondria-related pathway.
the nitric oxide-releasable spirolactone type diterpenoid compounds with apoptosis inducer activity could be developed as potential anticancer agents.
the NO-releasing spirotetronate-type diterpenoids (10a-f, 15a-f) could induce cell apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in Bel-7404 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NO-releasing spirollactone-type dierpenoids could be developed as a new class of antitumor agents.
we have synthesized and characterized two novel series of nitric oxide-releasable spirolactone diterpenoids.
the novel NO-releasing spirollactone-type diperenoid analogs are more potent than oridin and parent compound.
